draft.title: Environment
card: The environment is the living and non-living world around us. Living parts include plants, animals and people. Non-living parts include soil, water, air and rock.
People depend on the environment. It gives us things like water, food, air and materials to build with.
People also change the environment. Clearing land for farms or building a dam alters the plants, animals and water in an area.
The environment shapes how people live too. Climate and landforms can affect where people settle, what they eat and what they wear.
draft.remember: People depend on the environment, change it, and are shaped by it.

a.q: Which of these is a non-living part of the environment?
a.why: Water is a non-living part of the environment, along with soil, air and rock. Trees, birds and people are all living, so they are living parts. The mangrove tree might seem part of the land, but it is a living thing.

b.q: A town in the Northern Territory builds houses on tall stilts and uses wide verandahs because of heavy wet season rain and heat. What does this best show about people and the environment?
opts: The environment shapes how people live
People depend on the environment for food
People change the environment by clearing land
The environment is made only of living things
b.why: The climate affects how the houses are designed, so the environment is shaping how people live. People do build the houses, which changes the area a little. But the question is about why the design was chosen, and that comes from the environment's effect on people.
b.clue: Ask what caused the design choice: the people or the weather?

b.best: The environment shapes how people live
